Surah al-'Asr

Imam al-Shafi'i (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him) said: "This is a surah which, had nothing else been sent down to people but it, it would have sufficed them." This is the meaning of the words of another: "It encompasses all the sciences of the Qur'an. Its aim is to honor the human kind, created from a clinging clot ('alaq), and to explain its quintessence and distilled essence, namely the party that is saved on the Day of questioning about the purity of deeds, after alluding to their opposites; and to make known which deeds and states bring salvation, by abandoning what is perishing and turning to what is lasting, for it is the quintessence of the cosmos and the pith of existence. Its name, al-'Asr, is clear in this respect, for pressing ('asr) extracts the spirit of what is pressed and distinguishes its purity. For this reason the time of this final Prophet, who is the quintessence of creation, was the time of 'asr, and the 'Asr prayer was the best of the prayers. The explanation of how it contains the sciences of the Qur'an is by applying its sentences to what al-Ghazali said: 'The Qur'an is like an ocean containing islands (p-235) with six mines, four of them important. Two of the important ones are the most splendid ruby, whose red is knowledge of Allah, whose green is knowledge of His attributes, and whose blue is knowledge of His acts; and a green emerald, which is knowledge of the Last Day and what is in it. Two others are, first, a fresh pearl, which is knowledge of the acts of worship that bring one near to Him, Glorified and Exalted is He; and second, a fragrant musk, which is knowledge of the customary matters by which acts of worship are made ready. Two are completing: a great antidote (diryaq), which is knowledge of removing doubts, specious arguments and delusions, for they are poisons that destroy religion; and a grey ambergris, which is taking lesson from those who perished, by avoiding what caused their perishing, and following those who were saved, by following what caused their salvation.

The first sentence is for the ambergris, because in it one smells the scents of the perishing, and its opposite, the saved. It was placed first because warding off harms takes precedence over bringing benefits. The second sentence is for the ruby with its three qualities, and the emerald. The third is for the pearl and the musk, which are acts of worship that are intended, and customary matters that are a means extended toward them. The fourth is for the antidote, because specious arguments and doubts come only from idle delusions and false imaginings. The fifth is a means to them and completes them, because knowing that and avoiding it is achieved only by exerting effort in patience.'"

In the name of Allah, "besides whose Face everything perishes"; the Most Compassionate, "whose blessing embraced the righteous and the wicked, so nothing is like Him"; the Most Merciful, "who singled out His friends by perfecting the blessing, so they were a blaze of light upon the brow of time and a forehead for its people."

* *

(p-236) Since the apparent pleasure of this world is enjoying the goods in it, and since man will be questioned about what he has witnessed, the surah of rivalry in worldly increase (al-Takathur) closed by threatening with the sight of the Blazing Fire concerning that bliss. So the dweller of this abode is in utmost danger, and his bliss is in utmost turbidity. He said, indicating this, that most people are perishing, stressing it with an oath and a particle because of the denial by most people of that, whether in words or in conduct: ﴿By al-'Asr﴾, that is, the time in which their origin, Adam (peace be upon him), was created, which was in the late afternoon ('asr) of Friday, as stated in the sound hadith in Muslim; or the middle prayer, or its time, which is the era of the bearer of this Law, whose span in the time that has passed is like the time of 'asr in the day, or part of it; or the time of each person, which is the quintessence in relation to him, to alert him to its preciousness, pointing to seizing the chance to spend it in good out of fear of the Gathering; or the time of the late afternoon (asil), because it is the best of times, for what it holds of freedom from occupations, welcoming rest, and obtaining the benefit of what one spent that day, and for what it indicates of the length of the Hour, and the profit of one who has merchandise in it, with the ending of deeds and the folding up of the day, and it points to the Resurrection; or all of time, in which He, Glorified and Exalted, brought creatures into existence and decreed what is decreed, through the wonders that have appeared in it, which point to the might and (p-237) majesty of Allah the Exalted, calling to direct one's aspiration to Him and confine it to Him:

﴿Indeed, mankind﴾ that is, this kind (of creature), which is the noblest of kinds because it is in the best of forms, just as the 'asr (the age, or the time of the late afternoon) is the quintessence of time; and 'asr (pressing) is for extracting the quintessences of things. ﴿is in loss﴾ that is, in deficiency, in proportion to their endeavors in following their desires and spending their ages on their own aims, because of their natural inclination toward what is present, their turning away from what is absent, and their being deceived by what is perishing. This holds whether the loss is small or great, according to the variety among people, between the shrewd and the filthy. So whoever is a disbeliever is in ingratitude and disbelief (kufran), and whoever is a believer who is disobedient is in utter loss (khusran) if he is extreme in disobedience; otherwise he is in loss in the general sense, which is the meaning of the bare verbal noun (khusr). In this is an indication of the knowledge of the need for sending messengers, to make clear what is pleasing [to God] of beliefs, acts of worship and customs, in faith and submission (islam) and in persevering in that, so that whoever does it is among the People of the Right Hand, and whoever abandons it is among the People of the Left.

Al-Ustadh Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When He, the Exalted, said ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase diverts you﴾ [al-Takathur: 1], this included an indication of the shortsightedness of man and the confinement of his perception to the immediate, to the exclusion of the later (the Hereafter), in which lies his triumph and success. That is because of his distance from knowledge by the necessity of his nature: ﴿Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72]. The Glorified then informed us that this is the condition of man insofar as he is man, so He said ﴿By the 'asr﴾ [al-'Asr: 1] ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. So shortsightedness is his condition, injustice is his nature, and ignorance is his disposition. It is therefore fitting that rivalry in increase diverts him, and that God does not bring into him the spirit of faith ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-'Asr: 3] to the end of it. These are the ones whom

﴿neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of God﴾ [al-Nur: 37]. End of quotation.

Since a ruling on the genus is a ruling on all of its members, because by their own nature they have nothing but that, and since among them were those whom God (Glorified and Exalted is He) delivered from what man was created with, by placing them in the best of forms and preserving them from inclining toward the deficiencies within him, He excepted them. They are very few compared to the people of loss. So He said, indicating by the exception that souls call to evil and incline toward idleness and diversion, and that the sincere one is one in a thousand, as in the sound hadith: ﴿Except those who believe﴾, that is, those who have brought faith into being. Faith is the affirmation of what is known by necessity to have been brought by the Prophet (ﷺ): His oneness (Glorified and Exalted is He), and belief in His angels, His books, His messengers and the Last Day. Perhaps the wisdom of the past tense is to urge entry into the religion even at the lowest of ranks, and to give glad tidings to whoever does so, with its condition, of deliverance from loss.

Since man is a rational animal, and the perfection of his animality lies in the practical faculty, which moves by will and not by the compelling, bestial pull of desire, God Most High said: ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾, that is, in verification of the faith they affirmed. ﴿Righteous deeds﴾ means this genus: following the commands and avoiding the prohibitions, in acts of worship such as prayer and in customary dealings such as sale. By this they were Muslims after having been believers, so they bought the Hereafter with the world, and rivalry in worldly gain did not distract them. They won everlasting life and perpetual happiness, and no loss touched them.

[Since man, after perfecting himself through deeds, is not freed from loss absolutely] except by perfecting others, and at that point he becomes an heir, because the prophets (peace be upon them) were sent to perfect others; and since the religion does not stand, and when it stands is not completed, except through enjoining the good and forbidding the evil, which arises from the light of the heart, and this is not possible except through community, He said, singling out what is included in righteous deeds to draw attention to its greatness: ﴿and enjoin one another﴾, that is, some of them charge others, by word or by example, ﴿to the truth﴾, that is, the established matter. It is everything the Law has judged sound, so that it cannot rightly be denied in any respect, whether in speech, action, belief or anything else, in doing or in leaving. So they were doers of good. This is perfection in the practical faculty by bringing in what is good.

Since man is inclined toward deficiency, and the one who does that good is exposed to the hatred of the people of aggression, who are the majority in every age, God Most High said: ﴿and enjoin one another﴾, for man is energized by exhortation and benefits from a glance and a word, ﴿to patience﴾, that is, the patience that arises from the purification of the soul, in acting in obedience to God by upholding the truth, nullifying falsehood and rejecting it and its adherent, and patience in the harm that results from that, by avoiding evils until death, which is a cause that leads to the Abode of Peace. So they perfected the practical faculty and preserved the cognitive faculty that precedes it. That is the wisdom of acts of worship, for the wisdom of a thing is the goal and the intended benefit from it. Here there are two: one external to the doer, which is Paradise, and one internal, subsisting in him, which is the light that brings one near to the Truth (Glorified and Exalted is He). The expression "enjoining" (wasiyya) was chosen to point to gentleness in enjoining the good and forbidding the evil, and to using softness with the utmost effort. Patience is the quintessence of man, his secret, his purity, his cream and his extract, which is reached only when a person presses his own soul, compels it to acts of obedience and subdues it to keep to the Sunna and the community, until patience becomes, through training, a habit and a craft for it. Then its end embraces its beginning, and its joint connects with what joins it.

The surah is fourteen words, which points to the fourteenth year of prophethood, in which came the permission for jihad, which is the head of enjoining the good by deed, to manifest the truth. That is the year of the Hijra, in which its full moon was completed, its light and standing spread, and its might and victory abounded. If you add to it four words, the Basmala, it equals in number the fifth year after the Hijra, in which occurred the expedition of Badr al-Maw'id and the expedition of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). In both of them the most complete patience occurred from the Prophet (ﷺ) and then from those of the Companions (may God Most High be pleased with them) who agreed with him, to manifest truth and right. At Badr they were let down by the riders of 'Abd al-Qays, or by Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud and the agreement of the hypocrites, and they were frightened until terror and faintheartedness almost overtook them all. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"By God, I will go out even if no one goes out with me." And God revealed about it: ﴿Those to whom the people said, "Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them," but it increased them in faith and they said...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 173], the verses. At the Confederates, eyes turned away and hearts reached the throats, and the outcome of patience in it was revealed in what the Prophet (ﷺ) said when they left: "Now we raid them and they do not raid us." If you add to it the four pronouns, it points to the ninth year, in which occurred the expedition of Tabuk, the expedition of hardship, because of the severity in it, the outcome of whose patience was the arrival of the delegations, with the grandeur of might and fortune, and the succession of blessings, through the kindness of the Most Merciful, the Loving. By that he was the light of existence, and with the succession of favor and generosity from the God who is worshipped. May God send blessings upon our master Muhammad, his family and his Companions, the best of existence.
